scope: Deterministic ingredient-level safety lists used by the post-selection safety pass. They restrict what the selection layer may output; they never add an ingredient.

excludedFromSelection.reason: AICIS Evaluation Statement EVA00186 (26 June 2026) classifies retinal as a developmental toxicant (Reproductive toxicity Category 1B).

photosensitising.rule: Not allowed in a morning (AM) slot. CIR's Alpha Hydroxy Acids assessment advises sun protection because AHAs increase UV sensitivity; retinoids are conventionally applied in the evening.

highIntensityExfoliants.rule: Not allowed when the barrier guardrail is active (barrier, sensitivity or dryness context, or moderate/high self-reported reactivity).

retinal.note: AICIS Evaluation Statement EVA00186 (26 June 2026) classifies retinal as a developmental toxicant (Reproductive toxicity Category 1B).

citric-acid.note: Named by FDA as an AHA used in cosmetics.

salicylic-acid.note: CIR via FDA: formulate to avoid increased sun sensitivity; use sun protection.

mandelic-acid.note: Chemically an AHA but not named by FDA or CIR.

retinyl-palmitate.note: Increased skin neoplasms under simulated solar light in mice.

retinol.note: No photosensitivity source found for retinol; follows evening use convention and the tretinoin label's UV advice.

retinal.note: No photosensitivity source found; retinal is also excluded from selection (AICIS EVA00186).

glycolic-acid.note: Sources advise formulating to avoid irritation and stopping on irritation; none requires blocking on a weakened barrier.

gluconolactone.note: Polyhydroxy acid, milder than AHAs. Included as the strictest design choice; no source requires it.

tretinoin.note: Annex II entry 375; NPRA Appendix 7 entry 4 restricts supply to dermatologists.

isotretinoin.note: NPRA Appendix 7 entry 4: supply restricted to dermatologists; teratogenicity warning required.

hydroquinone.note: Pharmaceutical needing DCA registration; use under healthcare supervision.

adapalene.note: Differin 0.1% gel is registered as MAL20010011ARZ; the A suffix marks a prescription product (NPRA). Also listed as prescription-only by a licensed pharmacy.

tazarotene.note: No Malaysian registration (MAL number) found, so it cannot be sold in Malaysia; prescription-only where approved elsewhere.

trifarotene.note: Aklief Cream 50 mcg/g is registered as MAL24076001AZ; the A suffix marks a prescription product (NPRA).
